references.text: Contrast between blood ties and spiritual kinship: Joseph tests his biological brothers, while Jesus defines new brothers based on God's will.
The same theological contrast as in Mark 3:33; Jesus redefines kinship away from biology toward obedience to God.
Direct narrative connection: The verse summarizes the specific questions about father and brothers that Joseph asked earlier.
Direct continuation of the same speech: Describes the father's situation as the basis for the question about family.
Theological contrast in brotherhood: Cain kills his brother, while Joseph tests whether the brothers will now protect their brother.
